label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, poison-message, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER idempotent (unchanged), LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS retry -> dead_letter); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: poison-message
case.title: The ledger stops booking: a poison message
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer that retries unreadable messages forever (BAD_EVENTS=retry), then one unreadable event from the provider (a payment.updated with its amount as a decimal string): the ledger consumer is stuck on it, and books nothing behind it.
case.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to dead-lettering: the poison goes to the dead-letter topic, the backlog drains, and the money check passes again

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, messages up to it were not handled yet: ledger 127.

diagnosis.hypothesis: A poison message is blocking the ledger. Provider event evt_000282 (provider-events partition 1, offset 128, queued at about 07:45:15) has an amount that is not a positive integer number of cents. ledger-consumer was redeployed at 07:45:13 with BAD_EVENTS=retry. With that setting it retries the same message forever instead of setting it aside, so partition 1 makes no progress: attempt 9 and later, backing off to every 15 s. Every event behind offset 128 waits, and ledger lag grew from 0 to 177. The money check therefore cannot settle up to its cutoff, which fires BooksBehindProvider. payment-confirmer runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, so it dead-lettered the same event and kept going. That shows the event itself is malformed, and the setting decides whether it blocks the consumer. Still open: why the provider's event has a bad amount, and which settings ledger-consumer ran before 07:45:13. The deploy log shows only the current ones, so I am assuming the earlier BAD_EVENTS was not retry.

evidence.shows: Total consumer lag went from 0 at 07:44:19 to 1, then to 177 at 07:46:19. This confirms the books are falling behind.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 07:45:13, one minute before the alert, with BAD_EVENTS=retry. payment-confirmer runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter.
ledger-consumer logs repeated errors on provider-events/1@128, attempts 3 to 9: 'cannot book this event: amount must be positive integer cents', 'will retry the same message', backing off to 15 s.
payment-confirmer dead-lettered the same message, provider-events/1@128, at 07:45:15 for the same amount error.
The trace of evt_000282: the receiver queued it to partition 1, offset 128. The confirmer dead-lettered it. ledger-consumer failed it about 10 times over 75 s, with outcome will_retry each time.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings from before 07:45:13. Those are expected to dead-letter bad events, as payment-confirmer does. That unblocks partition 1 and lets the lag drain. Then investigate evt_000282's malformed amount with the provider and repair or replay it, so it gets booked correctly in the ledger and matched in the confirmer.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses briefly while it is recreated, and lag grows a little during that pause. Once rolled back, evt_000282 (and any similar bad events) goes to the dead letter queue and is not booked. The ledger will then differ from the provider for that event until someone repairs it. If the earlier settings also used BAD_EVENTS=retry, the rollback will not unblock the partition. In that case, change BAD_EVENTS to dead_letter in config instead.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with its current settings, LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry. The idempotent handler makes reprocessing safe.
